children: Scotiabank's Derek Holt reckons the latest data strongly suggests the Bank of Canada is behind the curve in fighting inflation. The consumer-price index dipped 0.1% on-month in August and was steady at 3% annually. However, Holt says traditional core CPI excluding food and energy landed at 3.9% on-month seasonally adjusted, annualized, which is the hottest since April 2025. The three-moving average is 3.6% on the same basis, and the four-month average is 3.6%, he adds. Core inflation is on a tear in Canada and that continues to support an interest rate increase at the Bank of Canada's October meeting, Holt argues. (robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)
